title.en: Volume 123 Biographies 48: Li, Xiao, Lu, Wei, Zhao, He
title.raw: 卷一百二十三 列傳第四十八 李蕭盧韋趙和 Volume 123 Biographies 48: Li, Xiao, Lu, Wei, Zhao, He

sentences.zh: 李蕭盧韋趙和

translations.literal: Li, Xiao, Lu, Wei, Zhao, and He.
translations.idiomatic: Li, Xiao, Lu, Wei, Zhao, and He.

sentences.zh: ◎李蕭盧韋趙和

translations.literal: ◎ Li, Xiao, Lu, Wei, Zhao, and He.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Li, Xiao, Lu, Wei, Zhao, and He.

sentences.zh: 李嶠，字巨山，趙州贊皇人。

translations.literal: Li Jiao, courtesy name Jushan, was a native of Zanhuang in Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiao, styled Jushan, came from Zanhuang in Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 早孤，事母孝。

translations.literal: He lost his father early and served his mother with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was devoted to his mother.

sentences.zh: 為兒時，夢人遺雙筆，自是有文辭，十五通《五經》，薛元超稱之。

translations.literal: As a child he dreamed that someone gave him a pair of writing brushes; from then on he had literary talent. At fifteen he mastered the Five Classics, and Xue Yuanchao praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood he dreamed that someone presented him with two brushes; thereafter he showed literary gifts. At fifteen he had mastered the Five Classics, and Xue Yuanchao spoke highly of him.

sentences.zh: 二十擢進士第，始調安定尉。

translations.literal: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination and was first appointed aide of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he took the jinshi degree and was first posted as aide of Anding.

sentences.zh: 舉制策甲科，遷長安。

translations.literal: He entered the policy-examination in the top grade and was transferred to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He placed in the top grade of the policy examination and was moved to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 時畿尉名文章者，駱賓王、劉光業，嶠最少，與等夷。

translations.literal: At that time among the metropolitan aides famed for literary composition were Luo Binwang and Liu Guangye; Jiao was the youngest yet ranked their equal.
translations.idiomatic: Among the capital aides then renowned for prose were Luo Binwang and Liu Guangye; Jiao was the youngest, yet he stood on equal footing with them.

sentences.zh: 授監察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 高宗擊邕、巖二州叛獠，詔監其軍，嶠入洞喻降之，由是罷兵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong attacked the rebellious Liao of Yong and Yan prefectures, he ordered Jiao to oversee the army; Jiao entered the caves to persuade them to submit, and the campaign was therefore halted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong campaigned against the rebel Liao of Yong and Yan, Jiao was ordered to supervise the forces; he entered their mountain strongholds to persuade surrender, and the troops were withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 稍遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 會來俊臣構狄仁傑、李嗣真、裴宣禮等獄，將抵死，敕嶠與大理少卿張德裕、侍御史劉憲覆驗，德裕等內知其冤，不敢異。

translations.literal: When Lai Junchen framed Di Renjie, Li Sizhen, Pei Xuanli, and others in a case for which they were to be put to death, the emperor ordered Jiao, together with Vice Minister of Justice Zhang Deyu and attendant censor Liu Xian, to review the case; Deyu and the others knew inwardly that the men were innocent but dared not dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen had framed Di Renjie, Li Sizhen, Pei Xuanli, and others in a capital case; as they were about to be executed, the throne ordered Jiao, Vice Minister of Justice Zhang Deyu, and attendant censor Liu Xian to re-examine the matter. Deyu and his colleagues knew the prisoners were innocent but dared not object.

sentences.zh: 嶠曰：「知其枉不申，是謂見義不為者。

translations.literal: Jiao said, "To know they are wronged yet not speak up is what is called seeing what is right and not doing it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao said, "To know men are wronged and yet not speak is to see what is right and fail to act.

sentences.zh: 」卒與二人列其枉，忤武後旨，出為潤州司馬。

translations.literal: " In the end he joined the two others in setting forth their wrongful conviction, offended Empress Wu's intent, and was sent out as secretary of Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " He finally joined the two others in reporting the injustice, ran counter to Empress Wu's wishes, and was demoted to secretary of Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久乃召為鳳閣舍人，文冊大號令，多主為之。

translations.literal: After a long while he was summoned as attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion, and most of the great edicts and proclamations were drafted under his direction.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was recalled as attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion; most of the great edicts and proclamations were composed under his hand.

sentences.zh: 初置右御史臺，察州縣吏善惡、風俗得失，嶠上疏曰：「禁網上疏，法象宜簡，簡則法易行而不煩雜，疏則所羅廣而不苛碎。

translations.literal: When the Right Censorate was first established to inspect the good and evil of prefectural and county officials and the gains and losses of local custom, Jiao submitted a memorial saying, "The prohibitory net should be loose above and the legal pattern kept simple; when simple, the law is easy to enforce without confusion, and when loose, what it covers is broad without petty minutiae.
translations.idiomatic: When the Right Censorate was first set up to scrutinize officials' conduct and local customs, Jiao memorialized: "The prohibitory net should be loose above and the law kept simple; simplicity makes enforcement easy and unburdensome, while looseness lets it cast wide without petty entanglement.

sentences.zh: 伏見垂拱時，諸道巡察使科條四十有四，至別敕令又三十。

translations.literal: I observe that in the Chui Gong era touring commissioners of the circuits had forty-four articles of regulation, and by separate edict there were thirty more.
translations.idiomatic: I note that under the Chui Gong reign touring commissioners already had forty-four regulatory articles, with thirty more added by separate edict.

sentences.zh: 而使以三月出，盡十一月奏事，每道所察吏，多者二千，少亦千計，要在品核才行而褒貶之。

translations.literal: Yet the commissioners set out in the third month and had to report by the eleventh; in each circuit the officials inspected numbered as many as two thousand or no fewer than a thousand, the aim being to assess conduct and talent for praise or blame.
translations.idiomatic: Yet commissioners departed in the third month and had to report by the eleventh; each circuit involved as many as two thousand officials under review, or no fewer than a thousand—the task being to grade conduct and talent for commendation or censure.

sentences.zh: 今期會迫促，奔逐不暇，欲望詳究所能，不亦艱哉。

translations.literal: Now deadlines press close and they rush about without respite; to expect them to examine everyone's capacity in detail—is that not arduous?
translations.idiomatic: With deadlines pressing and no respite from the chase, to expect a thorough inquiry into every man's capacity—is that not beyond reach?

sentences.zh: 此非隳於職，才有限，力不逮耳。

translations.literal: This is not a failure of duty but a limit of talent—the strength does not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: This is not dereliction but the limit of ability—their strength cannot match the charge.

sentences.zh: 臣願量其功程以為節制，使器周於用，力濟於時，然後得失可以精核矣。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to measure their workload and set bounds accordingly, so that capacity matches use and strength meets the time; only then can gains and losses be finely weighed.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that their workload be measured and bounded, so capacity fits the task and effort matches the season; only then can results be judged with precision.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「今所察按，準漢六條而推廣之，則無不包矣，烏在多張事目也？

translations.literal: " He also said, "What is now inspected and prosecuted, if extended on the model of the Han Six Articles, embraces everything—why multiply categories of matters?
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "If present inspections followed and extended the Han Six Articles, nothing would be left out—why multiply headings?

sentences.zh: 且朝廷萬機非無事，而機事之動，常在四方，故出使者冠蓋相望。

translations.literal: Moreover the court's myriad affairs are not without business, and when urgent matters arise they are usually in the four quarters; hence outgoing envoys follow one another in unbroken stream.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the court's myriad affairs are never idle, and when urgent business stirs it is usually in the provinces—hence the endless procession of outgoing envoys.

sentences.zh: 今已置使，則外州之事悉得專之，傳驛減矣。

translations.literal: Now that commissioners are in place, matters of the outer prefectures may all be entrusted to them, and relay traffic is reduced.
translations.idiomatic: With commissioners already in place, outer prefectures' affairs can be entrusted to them alone, and relay traffic is cut.

sentences.zh: 請率十州置一御史，以期歲為之限，容其身到屬縣，過閭裏，督察奸訛，采風俗，然後可課其成功。

translations.literal: I ask that one censor be set for every ten prefectures, with a term of one year as the limit, allowing him to reach subordinate counties in person, pass through hamlets, investigate wrongdoing, gather local custom, and only then assess his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Let one censor oversee every ten prefectures, with a one-year term, time enough to reach subordinate counties and walk the lanes, probe malfeasance, and take the pulse of custom—then his success may be judged.

sentences.zh: 且御史出入天禁，勵己自脩，比他吏相百也。

translations.literal: Moreover censors pass in and out of the heavenly precincts and discipline themselves in self-cultivation—a hundredfold beyond other officials.
translations.idiomatic: Censors moreover move within the imperial precincts and discipline themselves—a hundred times more than ordinary officers.

sentences.zh: 按劾回庸，糾擿隱欺，比他吏相十也。

translations.literal: In investigating and impeaching the corrupt and exposing hidden deceit they are tenfold beyond other officials.
translations.idiomatic: In impeaching the corrupt and exposing hidden fraud they are ten times more effective than others.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠用臣言，妙擇能者委之，莫不盡力效死矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly adopts my words and entrusts the task to men of outstanding ability, none will fail to exert themselves unto death.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly adopts this plan and entrusts able men with the charge, none will fail to serve unto death.

sentences.zh: 」武後善之，下制析天下為二十道，擇堪使者。

translations.literal: " Empress Wu approved it and issued an edict dividing the realm into twenty circuits and selecting suitable envoys.
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Wu approved the proposal and ordered the realm divided into twenty circuits with suitable envoys chosen.

sentences.zh: 為眾議沮止。

translations.literal: It was blocked by the opposition of many in council.
translations.idiomatic: Popular opposition in council blocked it.

sentences.zh: 俄知天宮侍郎事，進麟臺少監、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: Soon he was made acting vice minister of the Heavenly Office, advanced to vice director of the Unicorn Terrace, and made associate director of the Phoenix and Phoenix-Parrot Pavilions with the authority of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was acting vice minister of the Heavenly Office, then promoted to vice director of the Unicorn Terrace and made associate chief minister of the Phoenix and Phoenix-Parrot Pavilions.

sentences.zh: 遷鸞臺侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the Phoenix-Parrot Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved up to vice minister of the Phoenix-Parrot Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 會張錫輔政，嶠，其出也，罷為成均祭酒。

translations.literal: When Zhang Xi came to assist in government—Jiao being his rival—he was dismissed as libationer of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xi entered the government—Jiao being his rival—Jiao was removed and made libationer of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校文昌左丞，留守東都。

translations.literal: Soon he was made acting left vice director of the Literary Brilliance Office and left to guard the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was acting left vice director of the Literary Brilliance Office and left as guardian of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 長安三年，以本官復為平章事，知納言。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chang'an he resumed his former post as associate chief minister and took charge of the office of the chief censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an year three he again became associate chief minister in his former capacity and took charge of the chief censorate.

sentences.zh: 遷內史，嶠辭劇，復為成均祭酒、平章事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of the Secretariat; Jiao declined the heavy burden and again became libationer of the Directorate of Education while retaining associate chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to director of the Secretariat, Jiao declined the onerous post and again served as libationer of the Directorate of Education while remaining associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 武後將建大像於白司馬阪，嶠諫：「造像雖俾浮屠輸錢，然非州縣承辦不能濟，是名雖不稅而實稅之。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu was about to erect a great image at White Sima Slope, Jiao remonstrated: "Though the image-making lets the Buddhist clergy contribute money, it cannot be accomplished unless prefectures and counties undertake it—so though called no tax, in fact it is taxation.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu planned a great image at White Sima Slope, Jiao remonstrated: "Although the Buddha image lets clergy donate funds, prefectures and counties must carry it out—so though called no tax, it taxes in fact.

sentences.zh: 臣計天下編戶，貧弱者眾，有賣舍、帖田供王役者。

translations.literal: Your subject calculates that among registered households under Heaven the poor and weak are many; some sell their houses or pawn their fields to meet imperial corvée.
translations.idiomatic: I reckon that among registered households the poor are many—some sell homes or pawn fields to meet imperial labor levies.

sentences.zh: 今造像錢積十七萬緡，若頒之窮人，家給千錢，則紓十七萬戶饑寒之苦，德無窮矣。

translations.literal: The funds for the image now total one hundred seventy thousand strings of cash; if distributed to the destitute at a thousand cash per household, the hunger and cold of one hundred seventy thousand households would be relieved—virtue without end.
translations.idiomatic: Image funds now total one hundred seventy thousand strings; distributed to the destitute at a thousand per household, one hundred seventy thousand families would be spared hunger and cold—virtue without measure.

sentences.zh: 」不納。

translations.literal: " She did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: " She did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 張易之敗，坐附會貶豫州刺史，未行，改通州。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yizhi fell, Jiao was punished for association and demoted to prefect of Yu; before he departed he was changed to Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yizhi fell, Jiao was demoted for association to prefect of Yu; before he left he was reassigned to Tong.

sentences.zh: 數月，以吏部侍郎召，俄遷尚書。

translations.literal: After several months he was summoned as vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and soon promoted to minister.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he was recalled as vice minister of Personnel and soon made minister.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年，代韋安石為中書令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenlong he replaced Wei Anshi as director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong year two he replaced Wei Anshi as director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嶠在吏部時，陰欲藉時望復宰相，乃奏置員外官數千。

translations.literal: While Jiao was at the Ministry of Personnel he secretly wished to borrow contemporary esteem to return to the chancellorship and therefore memorialized to establish several thousand supernumerary offices.
translations.idiomatic: While at Personnel Jiao secretly hoped to ride popular esteem back to the chancellorship and memorialized for several thousand supernumerary posts.

sentences.zh: 既吏眾猥，府庫虛耗，乃上書歸咎於時，因蓋向非，曰：

translations.literal: Once officials were numerous and the treasury drained, he submitted a memorial blaming the times and thereby covering his former error, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Once offices swelled and the treasury emptied, he memorialized blaming the times and masking his earlier error, saying:

sentences.zh: 元首之尊，居有重門擊柝之衛，出有清警戒道之禁，所以備非常，息異望，誠不可易舉動，慢防閑也。

translations.literal: The dignity of the sovereign's head: at rest he has the guard of layered gates and night-watch clappers; abroad he has the prohibition of clear roads and cordoned processions—meant to prepare against the unexpected and quiet irregular hopes. Truly one must not lightly change his movements or relax precautions.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign's dignity requires layered gates and night watches at rest, cleared roads and cordons abroad—to guard against the unexpected and still irregular ambitions. His movements must not be made lightly nor precautions relaxed.

sentences.zh: 陛下厭崇邃，輕尊嚴，微服潛遊，閱廛過市，行路私議，朝廷驚懼，如禍產意外，縱不自惜，奈宗廟蒼生何？

translations.literal: Your Majesty dislikes lofty seclusion and treats solemn dignity lightly, going in disguise on secret excursions, passing through markets and shops; travelers whisper privately and the court is alarmed as if disaster might spring from nowhere. Even if you do not spare yourself, what of the ancestral temples and the living people?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty disdains lofty seclusion and treats dignity lightly, roaming in disguise through markets; wayfarers murmur and the court trembles as if calamity might strike unawares. Even if you spare yourself, what of the ancestral shrines and the people?

sentences.zh: 又分職建官，不可以濫。

translations.literal: Moreover in dividing duties and establishing offices one must not be excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover offices must not be multiplied without cause.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「官不必備，惟其人。

translations.literal: The tradition says, "Offices need not all be filled—only the right men matter.
translations.idiomatic: The tradition says, "Posts need not all be filled—only the right men matter.

sentences.zh: 」自帝室中興，以不慎爵賞為惠，冒級躐階，朝升夕改，正闕不給，加以員外。

translations.literal: " Since the imperial house's restoration, careless bestowal of ranks and rewards has been treated as kindness; men leap grades and steps, promoted in the morning and changed at evening; regular posts cannot be supplied and supernumeraries are added.
translations.idiomatic: " Since the dynasty's restoration, careless largesse in rank has been mistaken for kindness—men leap grades, promoted at dawn and shifted at dusk; regular posts cannot be filled and supernumeraries pile on.

sentences.zh: 內則府庫為殫，外則黎庶蒙害，非求賢助治之道也。

translations.literal: Within, the treasury is exhausted; without, the common people suffer harm—this is not the way to seek the worthy and aid governance.
translations.idiomatic: Within the treasury is drained; without the people suffer—this is not the way to seek talent and aid rule.

sentences.zh: 願愛晙班榮，息匪服之議。

translations.literal: I wish that morning and evening rank and glory be cherished and talk of improper appointments be stilled.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that rank and glory be granted with care and improper appointments cease.

sentences.zh: 今文武六十以上，而天造含容，皆矜恤之。

translations.literal: Now civil and military officials above sixty—the Heaven-made ruler is inclusive and compassionate toward them all.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials past sixty—the Heaven-made ruler is compassionate toward them all.

sentences.zh: 老病者已解還授，員外者既遣復留。

translations.literal: The old and ill have been released from office and returned to their posts, while supernumeraries dismissed are retained again.
translations.idiomatic: The old and sick have been released from office, yet dismissed supernumeraries are kept on again.

sentences.zh: 恐非所以消敝救時也。

translations.literal: I fear this is not the means to dispel exhaustion and rescue the times.
translations.idiomatic: I fear this will not dispel exhaustion nor rescue the times.

sentences.zh: 請敕有司料其可用進，不可用退。

translations.literal: I ask that the relevant offices be ordered to assess who may be advanced and who must be retired.
translations.idiomatic: Let the relevant offices advance the able and retire the unfit.

sentences.zh: 又遠方夷人不堪治事，國家向務撫納而官之，非立功酋長，類糜俸祿。

translations.literal: Moreover distant barbarians cannot manage affairs; the state has long sought to soothe and enroll them in office—yet unless they are chieftains who rendered merit, most merely consume salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Distant tribesmen cannot govern; the state has long enrolled them for appeasement—yet unless they are meritorious chieftains, most merely consume salaries.

sentences.zh: 願商度非要者，一切放還。

translations.literal: I wish that those judged nonessential be entirely sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Let all nonessential appointees be sent home.

sentences.zh: 又《易》稱：「何以守位曰仁，何以聚人曰財。

translations.literal: Moreover the Book of Changes says, "By what does one keep one's position? By benevolence. By what does one gather people? By wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes also says, "By what does one keep one's throne? By benevolence. By what does one gather the people? By wealth.

sentences.zh: 」今百姓乏窶，不安居處，不可以守位。

translations.literal: " Now the common people are impoverished and destitute, without secure dwellings—they cannot keep the throne.
translations.idiomatic: " The people are impoverished and unsettled—they cannot keep the throne.

sentences.zh: 倉儲蕩耗，財力傾殫，不足以聚人。

translations.literal: Granaries are emptied and resources exhausted—not enough to gather the people.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries are emptied and resources spent—not enough to gather the people.

sentences.zh: 山東病水潦，江左困輸轉。

translations.literal: East of the mountains suffers from floods; south of the Yangtze is strained by transport levies.
translations.idiomatic: The east suffers floods; the lower Yangtze region is strained by transport levies.

sentences.zh: 國匱於上，人窮於下。

translations.literal: The state is depleted above and the people exhausted below.
translations.idiomatic: The state is depleted above and the people exhausted below.

sentences.zh: 如令邊埸少曌，恐逋亡遂多，盜賊群行，何財召募？

translations.literal: If the frontier should see even a little disturbance, I fear fugitives will multiply and bandits roam in packs—what wealth to recruit troops?
translations.idiomatic: If the frontier stirs even slightly, fugitives will multiply and bandits gather—what wealth remains to raise troops?

sentences.zh: 何眾閑遏乎？

translations.literal: What multitude to restrain them?
translations.idiomatic: What force to hold them back?

sentences.zh: 又崇作寺觀，功費浩廣。

translations.literal: Moreover temples and monasteries are lavishly built at vast expense.
translations.idiomatic: Temples and monasteries are raised at vast expense.

sentences.zh: 今山東歲饑，糟糠不厭。

translations.literal: Now east of the mountains there is famine yearly and coarse chaff is not disdained.
translations.idiomatic: East of the mountains famine reigns and even chaff is welcome.

sentences.zh: 而投艱厄之會，收庸、調之半，用籲嗟之物，以榮土木，恐怨結三靈，謗蒙四海。

translations.literal: Yet in this time of hardship half the corvée and tax levies are taken and lamentation is turned to glorify timber and stone—I fear resentment will bind the three spirits and slander cover the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in hardship half the corvée and tax levies are taken and the people's lamentations turned to glorify timber and stone—I fear the spirits will resent it and slander will spread across the realm.

sentences.zh: 又比緣征戍，巧詐百情，破役隱身，規脫租賦。

translations.literal: Moreover of late because of military campaigns cunning deceit takes a hundred forms—breaking corvée to hide one's person and scheming to escape taxes and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Lately military campaigns have bred a hundred forms of fraud—evading corvée by concealment and scheming to escape taxes.

sentences.zh: 今道人私度者幾數十萬，其中高戶多丁，黠商大賈，詭作臺符，羼名偽度。

translations.literal: Now those privately ordained as Daoist clergy number nearly several hundred thousand; among them wealthy households with many sons, shrewd merchants and great traders forge imperial tallies and insert names for false ordination.
translations.idiomatic: Privately ordained clergy now number nearly a hundred thousand—wealthy households with many sons, shrewd merchants forging imperial tallies for false ordination.

sentences.zh: 且國計軍防，並仰丁口，今丁皆出家，兵悉入道，征行租賦，何以備之？

translations.literal: Moreover state revenue and military defense both depend on registered males; now males all leave the household and soldiers all enter the clergy—how are campaigns and taxes to be supplied?
translations.idiomatic: State revenue and defense both depend on registered males; now males take orders and soldiers enter the clergy—how will campaigns and taxes be met?

sentences.zh: 又重賂貴近，補府若史，移沒籍產，以州縣甲等更為下戶。

translations.literal: Moreover by heavy bribes to the powerful near the throne men are appointed as prefectural clerks; registered property is seized and reassigned, and households ranked by prefecture and county are reclassified as lower grades.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy bribes to court favorites win prefectural clerkships; registered property is seized and household grades lowered by bribery.

sentences.zh: 當道城鎮，至無捉驛者，役逮小弱，即破其家。

translations.literal: In towns along the main routes there are sometimes none left to man relay stations; when corvée reaches the small and weak, their households are ruined at once.
translations.idiomatic: Along main routes towns sometimes lack men even for relay stations; when corvée falls on the weak, households are ruined at once.

sentences.zh: 願許十道使訪察括取，使奸猾不得而隱。

translations.literal: I wish that commissioners of the ten circuits be permitted to investigate and register them so that the cunning cannot hide.
translations.idiomatic: Let commissioners of the ten circuits investigate and register them so the cunning cannot hide.

sentences.zh: 又太常樂戶已多，復求訪散樂，獨持大鼓者已二萬員，願量留之，余勒還籍，以杜妄費。

translations.literal: Moreover the household musicians of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices are already numerous, yet a search is made for scattered performers; those who hold only the great drum already number twenty thousand. I wish that a measured number be retained and the rest compelled to return to registration to stop wasteful spending.
translations.idiomatic: Court musicians are already numerous, yet scattered performers are sought—drummers alone number twenty thousand. Retain a measured corps and return the rest to registration to stop waste.

sentences.zh: 中宗以嶠身宰相，乃自陳失政，丐罷官，無所嫁非，手詔詰讓。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong, since Jiao himself was chancellor, took his self-accusation of misgovernment and plea to resign as blaming others with no basis; he issued a handwritten edict rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong, Jiao being chancellor himself, took his confession of misrule and plea to resign as blame-shifting without cause and rebuked him by handwritten edict.

sentences.zh: 嶠惶恐，復視事。

translations.literal: Jiao was fearful and resumed his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao was alarmed and resumed office.

sentences.zh: 三年，加修文館大學士，封趙國公，以特進同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made grand academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, and given the special advancement of third rank equal to the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he was made grand academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature, enfeoffed Duke of Zhao, and given third rank equal to the Secretariat and Chancellery as special advancement.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，罷政事，下除懷州刺史，致仕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong acceded, Jiao was removed from government affairs, demoted to prefect of Huai, and granted retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong acceded, Jiao left government, was demoted to prefect of Huai, and retired.

sentences.zh: 初，中宗崩，嶠嘗密請相王諸子不宜留京師。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Zhongzong died, Jiao had secretly memorialized that the Prince of Xiang's sons ought not remain in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at Emperor Zhongzong's death, Jiao had secretly urged that the Prince of Xiang's sons should not remain in the capital.

sentences.zh: 及玄宗嗣位，獲其表宮中，或請誅之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong succeeded, his memorial was found in the palace and some asked that he be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong succeeded, the memorial was found in the palace and some called for his execution.

sentences.zh: 張說曰：「嶠誠懵逆順，然為當時謀，吠非其主，不可追罪。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue said, "Jiao was indeed confused about what accords and what rebels, yet he acted as counsel for his own time; a dog barks at one who is not its master—past fault cannot be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue said, "Jiao was indeed confused about loyalty, yet he advised for his own day; a dog barks at whoever is not its master—past fault should not be punished.

sentences.zh: 」天子亦顧數更赦，遂免，貶滁州別駕，聽隨子虔州刺史暢之官。

translations.literal: " The Son of Heaven also considered the many amnesties since and pardoned him, demoting him to vice prefect of Chu and permitting him to follow his son Chang, prefect of Qian, to his post.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor also weighed repeated amnesties and spared him, demoting him to vice prefect of Chu with permission to accompany his son Chang, prefect of Qian, to his post.

sentences.zh: 改廬州別駕，卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He was changed to vice prefect of Lu and died at seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Reassigned to vice prefect of Lu, he died at seventy.

sentences.zh: 嶠富才思，有所屬綴，人多傳諷。

translations.literal: Jiao was rich in literary talent; whatever he composed people widely circulated and recited.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao was richly gifted; whatever he wrote people circulated and recited.

sentences.zh: 武後時，汜水獲瑞石，嶠為御史，上《皇符》一篇，為世譏薄。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time a propitious stone was found at Sishui; Jiao, as censor, submitted a piece entitled "Imperial Talisman," for which the age mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu a propitious stone was found at Sishui; Jiao, then censor, submitted "Imperial Talisman"—for which the age mocked him.

sentences.zh: 然其仕前與王勃、楊盈川接，中與崔融、蘇味道齊名，晚諸人沒，而為文章宿老，一時學者取法焉。

translations.literal: Yet in his early career he associated with Wang Bo and Yang Yingchuan; in mid-career he was famed alongside Cui Rong and Su Weidao; in late years, after the others had died, he became the senior master of letters, and scholars of the time took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Yet early he moved in Wang Bo's circle and Yang Yingchuan's; mid-career he stood with Cui Rong and Su Weidao; in old age, after the others had passed, he was the senior master of letters whom scholars emulated.

sentences.zh: 蕭至忠，沂州丞人。

translations.literal: Xiao Zhizhong was a native of Cheng in Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhizhong came from Cheng in Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖德言，為秘書少監。

translations.literal: His grandfather Deyan was vice director of the Secretariat Archives.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Deyan was vice director of the Secretariat Archives.

sentences.zh: 至忠少與友期諸路，會雨雪，人引避，至忠曰：「寧有與人期可以失信？

translations.literal: Zhizhong in youth had arranged to meet a friend on the road; when rain and snow came people urged him to take shelter, but Zhizhong said, "How can one keep an appointment with another yet break faith?
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Zhizhong had arranged to meet a friend on the road; when snow fell people urged shelter, but he said, "How can one keep an appointment and break faith?

sentences.zh: 」卒友至乃去，眾嘆服。

translations.literal: " He left only when his friend arrived; the crowd sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: " He left only when his friend arrived; onlookers marveled.

sentences.zh: 仕為伊闕、洛陽尉。

translations.literal: In office he served as aide of Yique and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as aide of Yique and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 遷監察御史，劾奏鳳閣侍郎蘇味道贓貪，超拜吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to investigating censor, impeached Vice Minister Su Weidao of the Phoenix Pavilion for corruption, and was specially advanced to vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted investigating censor, he impeached Vice Minister Su Weidao of the Phoenix Pavilion for graft and was specially advanced to vice director of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 至忠長擊斷，譽聞當時。

translations.literal: Zhizhong excelled in decisive judgment and his reputation was known in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong was famed for decisive judgment.

sentences.zh: 中宗神龍初，為御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong under Emperor Zhongzong he became chief investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shenlong under Emperor Zhongzong he became chief investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 始，至忠為御史，而李承嘉為大夫，嘗讓諸御史曰：「彈事有不咨大夫，可乎？

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhizhong was a censor and Li Chengjia was chief censor, Chengjia once reproved the censors saying, "Can impeachments be submitted without consulting the chief censor?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhizhong was a censor under chief censor Li Chengjia, Chengjia once reproved the censors: "Can impeachments go forward without consulting the chief?

sentences.zh: 」眾不敢對，至忠獨曰：「故事，臺無長官。

translations.literal: " None dared reply; only Zhizhong said, "By precedent the censorate has no superior officer.
translations.idiomatic: " None replied; only Zhizhong said, "By precedent the censorate has no superior officer.

sentences.zh: 御史，天子耳目也，其所請奏當專達，若大夫許而後論，即劾大夫者，又誰白哉？

translations.literal: Censors are the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears; what they memorialize should reach him directly. If the chief censor must approve before submission, then who will report the chief censor when he is impeached?
translations.idiomatic: Censors are the emperor's eyes and ears; their memorials should reach him directly. If the chief must approve first, who will report the chief when he is impeached?

sentences.zh: 」承嘉慚。

translations.literal: " Chengjia was ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengjia was shamed.

sentences.zh: 至是，承嘉為戶部尚書，至忠劾祝欽明、竇希玠與承嘉等罪，百寮震悚。

translations.literal: Now Chengjia was minister of revenue; Zhizhong impeached Zhu Qinming, Dou Xijie, and Chengjia and others for crimes, and the hundred officials trembled in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Now Chengjia was minister of revenue; Zhizhong impeached Zhu Qinming, Dou Xijie, Chengjia, and others—the whole court trembled.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，猶兼中丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, still concurrently serving as chief investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of Personnel while continuing as chief investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 節湣太子以兵誅武三思而敗，宗楚客等諗侍御史冉祖雍上變，言相王與太子謀。

translations.literal: The Jiemin Crown Prince failed in raising troops to kill Wu Sansi; Zong Chuke and others incited attendant censor Ran Zuyong to report an emergency, saying the Prince of Xiang had plotted with the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Jiemin failed in his armed attempt to kill Wu Sansi, Zong Chuke and others persuaded attendant censor Ran Zuyong to submit an urgent report alleging that the Prince of Xiang had conspired with the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 帝欲按之，至忠泣曰：「往者，天後欲以相王為太子，而王不食累日，獨請迎陛下，其讓德天下莫不聞。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to investigate; Zhizhong wept and said, "Formerly, when the empress wished to make the Prince of Xiang crown prince, the prince went without food for days and alone asked to welcome Your Majesty back—his humility and virtue were heard throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to pursue the matter, but Zhizhong wept and said, "In the past, when the empress wished to make the Prince of Xiang crown prince, he refused food for days and insisted on welcoming Your Majesty back. His humility and virtue were known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 陛下貴為天子，不能容一弟，受人羅織耶？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, exalted as Son of Heaven, cannot tolerate one younger brother and accepts others' fabrications?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty stands exalted as Son of Heaven—can you not tolerate one younger brother and instead accept others' fabricated charges?

sentences.zh: 竊為陛下不取。

translations.literal: I privately consider this unworthy for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I privately believe this would be unworthy of Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」帝納其言，止。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice and dropped the investigation.

sentences.zh: 尋授中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and associate director of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed vice director of the Secretariat with the concurrent title of associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 上疏陳時政曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial setting forth the affairs of the time, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on current affairs, stating:

sentences.zh: 求治之道，首於用賢。

translations.literal: The way to seek good governance begins with employing the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The path to good governance begins with appointing worthy men.

sentences.zh: 茍非其才則官曠，官曠則事廢，事廢則人殘，歷代所以陵遲者此也。

translations.literal: If not their talent, then offices are empty; if offices are empty, then affairs are abandoned; if affairs are abandoned, then people are harmed—this is why dynasties through the ages have declined.
translations.idiomatic: When the unfit hold office, posts go unfilled by capable men; when capable men are absent, affairs are neglected; when affairs are neglected, the people suffer. This is how dynasties have declined through the ages.

sentences.zh: 今授職用人，多因貴要為粉飾，上下相蒙，茍得為是。

translations.literal: Now in granting posts and employing men, many rely on the powerful and influential for ornament; superiors and subordinates deceive one another, and mere attainment is taken as sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Today appointments are made largely to flatter the powerful and well connected; superiors and subordinates deceive one another, and mere self-advancement is treated as enough.

sentences.zh: 夫官爵，公器也；

translations.literal: For offices and ranks are public instruments;
translations.idiomatic: For offices and ranks are instruments of the public good;

sentences.zh: 恩幸，私惠也。

translations.literal: favor and patronage are private benefits.
translations.idiomatic: while favor and patronage are private benefits.

sentences.zh: 王者正可金帛富之，梁肉食之，以存私澤也。

translations.literal: A ruler may properly enrich them with gold and silk and feed them with fine grain and meat, thereby preserving private goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler may properly enrich favorites with gold and silk and feed them with fine food, thereby maintaining a private bond of goodwill.

sentences.zh: 若公器而私用之，則公義不行而勞人解體，私謁開而正言塞。

translations.literal: If public instruments are used privately, then public duty is not carried out and laboring people are disheartened; private petitions open while upright words are blocked.
translations.idiomatic: But if public office is used for private ends, public duty fails and working people lose heart; private petitions flourish while honest counsel is silenced.

sentences.zh: 日朘月削，卒見雕弊。

translations.literal: Day by day eroded, month by month cut away, at last utter exhaustion appears.
translations.idiomatic: Resources are eroded day by day and cut away month by month, until the state is utterly drained.

sentences.zh: 今列位已廣，冗員復倍。

translations.literal: Now the ranks are already broad, and redundant appointees again double.
translations.idiomatic: The ranks of office are already numerous, and redundant appointees have doubled again.

sentences.zh: 陛下降不呰之澤，近戚有無涯之請，臺閣之內，朱紫充滿，官秩益輕，恩賞彌數。

translations.literal: Your Majesty bestows ungrudging bounty; close kin have boundless requests; within the halls of office, crimson and purple fill every seat—ranks grow ever lighter, and favors and rewards ever more frequent.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty dispenses ungrudging largess, while close relatives make endless demands. Within the halls of government, crimson and purple robes crowd every seat—ranks grow ever cheaper, and rewards ever more frequent.

sentences.zh: 才者不用，用者不才，故人不效力，官匪其人，欲求治固難矣。

translations.literal: The talented are not used; those used are not talented—hence men do not exert effort, and offices do not match their holders; to seek good governance is indeed difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The talented go unused, and those who are used lack talent. Men therefore exert no effort, and offices do not match their holders. Under such conditions, good governance is indeed hard to achieve.

sentences.zh: 又宰相要官子弟，多居美爵，並罕才藝，而更相諉托。

translations.literal: Moreover, sons of chancellors and important officials mostly hold fine ranks, yet rarely possess talent or skill, and instead recommend and entrust one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the sons of chancellors and high officials mostly hold fine ranks, yet rarely possess real ability, and instead take turns recommending and protecting one another.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「私人之子，百寮是試。

translations.literal: The Book of Odes says, "The sons of favorites—let all the hundred offices try them.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says, "The sons of favorites—let all the hundred offices try them.

sentences.zh: 或以其酒，不以其漿，鞙鞙佩遂，不以其長。

translations.literal: They may offer their wine but not their water; their tinkling girdle-pendants hang full, yet not by their own length."
translations.idiomatic: They may offer their wine but not their water; their tinkling girdle-pendants hang full, yet not by their own merit."

sentences.zh: 」此言王政不平而眾官廢職，私家子列試榮班，徒長其佩爾。

translations.literal: This speaks of royal government being unjust and all officials neglecting their duties—sons of private favorites parade through honorary ranks, merely lengthening their sashes and pendants, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: This describes a time when royal government was unjust and officials neglected their duties—sons of private favorites were placed in honorary ranks, lengthening their sashes and pendants and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下愛惜爵賞，官無虛授，進大雅以樞近，退小人於閑左，使政令惟一，私不害公，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to cherish offices and rewards, appoint no office in vain, advance great men of integrity to posts near the pivot, retire petty men to idle stations, make government commands unified and private interest not harm the public good—then all under Heaven would be greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to value offices and rewards and appoint no post in vain: advance men of true integrity to positions near the center of power, and retire petty men to idle posts, so that government commands may be unified and private interest may not harm the public good. Then all under Heaven would be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 且貞觀故事，宰相子弟多居外職，非直抑強宗，亦以擇賢才爾。

translations.literal: Moreover, by the precedent of the Zhenguan era, sons of chancellors mostly held outside posts—not only to restrain powerful clans, but also to select men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, under the precedent of the Zhenguan reign, the sons of chancellors mostly held posts outside the capital—not only to restrain powerful clans, but also to select men of talent.

sentences.zh: 請自宰相及諸司長官子弟，並授外官，共寧百性，表裏相統。

translations.literal: I request that sons of chancellors and section chiefs alike be appointed to outside posts, together to bring peace to the hundred surnames, with inner and outer ranks mutually regulated.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the sons of chancellors and department chiefs alike be appointed to outside posts, so that together they may bring peace to the people and inner and outer offices may be properly coordinated.

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept the proposal.

sentences.zh: 俄為侍中、中書令。

translations.literal: Soon he became palace attendant and director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made palace attendant and director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時楚客懷奸植黨，而韋巨源、楊再思、李嶠務自安，無所弼正，至忠介其間，獨不詭隨，時望翕然歸重。

translations.literal: At the time Zong Chuke harbored treachery and built factions; Wei Juyuan, Yang Zaisi, and Li Jiao sought only their own security and offered no correction; Zhizhong stood among them, alone not bending and following—public esteem swiftly gathered to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zong Chuke harbored treachery and built factions, while Wei Juyuan, Yang Zaisi, and Li Jiao sought only their own safety and offered no corrective counsel. Zhizhong stood among them, refusing alone to bend and follow, and public esteem quickly gathered around him.

sentences.zh: 帝亦曰：「宰相中，至忠最憐我。

translations.literal: The emperor also said, "Among the chancellors, Zhizhong cares for me the most."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also said, "Among the chancellors, Zhizhong cares for me the most."

sentences.zh: 」韋後嘗為其弟洵與至忠殤女冥婚。

translations.literal: Empress Wei once arranged a posthumous marriage between her brother Xun and Zhizhong's deceased daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei once arranged a posthumous marriage between her brother Xun and Zhizhong's daughter, who had died young.

sentences.zh: 至忠又以女妻後舅崔從禮子無诐。

translations.literal: Zhizhong in turn gave his daughter in marriage to Empress Wei's maternal uncle Cui Congli's son Wu Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong in turn gave his daughter in marriage to Wu Bi, son of Cui Congli, the empress's maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 兩家合禮，帝主蕭，後主崔，時謂「天子嫁女，皇后娶婦。」

translations.literal: When the two families joined in marriage rites, the emperor presided over Xiao's side and the empress over Cui's—at the time people called it "the Son of Heaven giving away a daughter while the empress takes a bride."
translations.idiomatic: When the two families performed the marriage rites, the emperor presided on Xiao's side and the empress on Cui's. People at the time said, "The Son of Heaven is giving away a daughter while the empress is taking a bride."

sentences.zh: 至忠始在朝，有風望，容止閑敏，見推為名臣。

translations.literal: When Zhizhong first entered court, he had reputation and bearing; his appearance and demeanor were calm and quick-witted, and he was pushed as a famous minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhizhong first entered court, he enjoyed reputation and prestige. Calm and quick-witted in bearing and manner, he was acclaimed as a distinguished minister.

sentences.zh: 外方直，糾擿不法，而內無守，觀時輕重而去就之。

translations.literal: Outwardly he was upright and direct, investigating and exposing violations of law; inwardly he lacked constancy, gauging the times' weight and lightness in deciding where to go and where to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he was upright and direct, investigating and exposing illegal conduct; inwardly he lacked firm principle, weighing the times and shifting his allegiance accordingly.

sentences.zh: 始為御史，桓彥範等頗引重。

translations.literal: When he first served as censor, Huan Yanfan and others greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: When he first served as a censor, Huan Yanfan and others held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 五王失政，更因武三思得中丞，附安樂公主為宰相。

translations.literal: When the Five Princes lost power, he again gained the post of chief investigating censor through Wu Sansi, attached himself to Princess Anle, and became chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After the Five Princes lost power, he again obtained the post of chief investigating censor through Wu Sansi, attached himself to Princess Anle, and became chancellor.

sentences.zh: 及韋氏敗，遽發韋洵壟，持其女柩歸。

translations.literal: When the Wei clan fell, he hastily opened Wei Xun's tomb and brought back his daughter's coffin.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei clan fell, he hastily opened Wei Xun's tomb and brought back his daughter's coffin.

sentences.zh: 後依太平，復當國。

translations.literal: Later he relied on Princess Taiping and again held the reins of government.
translations.idiomatic: Later he relied on Princess Taiping and again held power at court.

sentences.zh: 嘗出主第，遇宋璟，璟戲曰：「非所望於蕭傅。

translations.literal: Once, leaving the princess's mansion, he met Song Jing; Song jestingly said, "This is not what was expected of Minister Xiao."
translations.idiomatic: Once, leaving the princess's residence, he met Song Jing, who said in jest, "This is not what was expected of you, Minister Xiao."

sentences.zh: 」至忠曰：「善乎，宋生之言。

translations.literal: Zhizhong said, "Well said, Master Song."
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong replied, "Well said, Master Song."

sentences.zh: 」然不能自返也。

translations.literal: Yet he could not return to his former path.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he could not turn back.

sentences.zh: 娣嫁蔣欽緒，欽緒每戒之，至忠不聽。

translations.literal: His younger sister married Jiang Qinxu; Qinxu repeatedly admonished him, but Zhizhong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: His younger sister was married to Jiang Qinxu, who repeatedly warned him, but Zhizhong would not listen.

sentences.zh: 嘆曰：「九世卿族，一舉而滅之，可哀也已！

translations.literal: Jiang sighed and said, "A ministerial clan of nine generations—destroyed in a single stroke. How lamentable!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiang sighed and said, "A ministerial clan of nine generations—destroyed in a single stroke. How lamentable!"

sentences.zh: 」不喜接賓客，以簡儉自高，故生平奉賜，無所遺施，及籍沒，珍寶不可計。

translations.literal: He disliked receiving guests and prided himself on simplicity and frugality; hence throughout his life his received gifts went nowhere in largesse—yet when his property was confiscated, treasures beyond counting were found.
translations.idiomatic: He disliked receiving guests and prided himself on simplicity and frugality. Throughout his life he gave away none of the gifts he received, yet when his property was confiscated, treasures beyond counting were discovered.

sentences.zh: 然玄宗賢其為人，後得源乾曜，亟用之，謂高力士曰：「若知吾進乾曜遽乎？

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Xuanzong admired his character; when he later obtained Yuan Qianyao and promptly employed him, he said to Gao Lishi, "Do you know why I advanced Qianyao so quickly?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperor Xuanzong admired Zhizhong's character. When he later obtained Yuan Qianyao and promptly employed him, he said to Gao Lishi, "Do you know why I promoted Qianyao so quickly?

sentences.zh: 吾以其貌言似蕭至忠。

translations.literal: Because his appearance and speech resembled Xiao Zhizhong."
translations.idiomatic: Because his appearance and speech reminded me of Xiao Zhizhong."

sentences.zh: 」力士曰：「彼不嘗負陛下乎？

translations.literal: Lishi said, "Did he not once betray Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: Lishi said, "Did he not once betray Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「至忠誠國器，但晚謬爾，其始不謂之賢哉？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Zhizhong was a treasure of the state in loyalty—but in his later years he went astray; was he not called worthy at the start?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Zhizhong was a treasure of the state, though in his later years he went astray. Was he not regarded as worthy in his early days?"

sentences.zh: 弟元嘉，工部侍郎；

translations.literal: Younger brother Yuanjia was vice director of the Ministry of Works;
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yuanjia served as vice minister of Works;

sentences.zh: 廣微，工部員外郎。

translations.literal: Guangwei was assistant director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: and Guangwei served as assistant director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 盧藏用，字子潛，幽州范陽人。

translations.literal: Lu Cangyong, courtesy name Ziqian, was a native of Fanyang in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cangyong, styled Ziqian, came from Fanyang in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 父敬，魏州長史，號才吏。

translations.literal: His father Jing was prefectural secretary of Weizhou and was called a capable official.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing served as prefectural secretary of Weizhou and was known as a capable administrator.

sentences.zh: 藏用能屬文，舉進士，不得調。

translations.literal: Cangyong could compose prose; he passed the jinshi examination but received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Cangyong was skilled at literary composition. He passed the jinshi examination but received no appointment.

sentences.zh: 與兄徵明偕隱終南、少室二山，學練氣，為辟谷，登衡、廬，仿徉岷、峨。

translations.literal: Together with his elder brother Zhengming he went into seclusion on Mount Zhongnan and Mount Shaoshi, studied breath cultivation and practiced abstaining from grain; he climbed Mount Heng and Mount Lu and wandered freely among Mount Min and Mount Emei.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his elder brother Zhengming, he went into seclusion on Mount Zhongnan and Mount Shaoshi, studied breath cultivation, and practiced grain abstention. He climbed Mount Heng and Mount Lu and wandered freely among Mount Min and Mount Emei.

sentences.zh: 與陳子昂、趙貞固友善。

translations.literal: He was on friendly terms with Chen Zi'ang and Zhao Zhengong.
translations.idiomatic: He was on friendly terms with Chen Zi'ang and Zhao Zhengong.

sentences.zh: 長安中，召授左拾遺。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era, he was summoned and appointed left reminder.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an reign he was summoned and appointed left reminder.

sentences.zh: 武後作興泰宮於萬安山，上疏諫曰：「陛下離宮別觀固多矣，又窮人力以事土木，臣恐議者以陛下為不愛人而奉己也。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu built Xingtai Palace on Mount Wan'an, he submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying, "Your Majesty already has many detached palaces and villa estates; now you exhaust human labor for building projects—I fear commentators will take Your Majesty to be one who does not love the people but serves himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu built Xingtai Palace on Mount Wan'an, he submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying, "Your Majesty already has many detached palaces and villa estates, yet now you exhaust human labor on building projects. I fear people will say that Your Majesty does not love the people but serves only yourself.

sentences.zh: 且頃歲谷雖頗登，而百姓未有儲。

translations.literal: Moreover, though harvests in recent years have been fairly abundant, the common people have not yet stored grain.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though harvests in recent years have been fairly good, the common people still have no reserves.

sentences.zh: 陛下巡幸，訖靡休息，斤斧之役，歲月不空，不因此時施德布化，而又廣宮苑，臣恐下未易堪。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's tours and visitations have hardly ceased; the work of axe and adze knows no idle month—if at such a time you do not spread virtue and transform the realm, but instead expand palaces and gardens, I fear those below will find it hard to bear.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's tours and visitations have scarcely ceased, and the work of axe and adze knows no idle month. If at such a time you do not spread virtue and transform the realm, but instead expand palaces and gardens, I fear the people below will find it hard to endure.

sentences.zh: 今左右近臣，以諛意為忠，犯忤為患，至令陛下不知百姓失業，百姓亦不知左右傷陛下之仁也。

translations.literal: Today the close attendants at your side treat flattery as loyalty and regard giving offense as disaster—so that Your Majesty does not know the people's loss of livelihood, and the people likewise do not know how your attendants wound Your Majesty's benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Today your close attendants treat flattery as loyalty and regard giving offense as disaster, so that Your Majesty does not know the people's loss of livelihood, and the people likewise do not know how those attendants wound Your Majesty's benevolence.

sentences.zh: 忠臣不避誅震以納君於仁，明主不惡切詆以趨名於後。

translations.literal: Loyal ministers do not shun execution and punishment to lead their lord toward benevolence; enlightened rulers do not loathe blunt criticism to win a good name in posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers do not shrink from execution and punishment in order to lead their ruler toward benevolence, and enlightened rulers do not hate blunt criticism in order to win a good name in posterity.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能發明制，以勞人為辭，則天下必以為愛力而苦己也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty could indeed proclaim a clear edict, citing the burden on the people as your reason, then all under Heaven would surely take it as loving the people's strength while chastening yourself.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would truly issue a clear edict, citing the burden on the people as your reason, then all under Heaven would surely regard it as loving the people's strength and chastening yourself.

sentences.zh: 不然，下臣此章，得與執事者共議。

translations.literal: Otherwise, let this memorial of your lowly servant be discussed together with those in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, let this memorial of your humble servant be discussed together with those in charge.

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: She did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: She did not accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 姚元崇持節靈武道，奏為管記。

translations.literal: When Yao Yuanchong held commission for the Lingwu circuit, Lu was memorialized for appointment as recording secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Yuanchong held commission for the Lingwu circuit, Lu was recommended and appointed recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 還應縣令舉，甲科，為濟陽令。

translations.literal: Upon returning he responded to the magistrate recommendation, received top grade, and became magistrate of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Upon returning, he responded to a magistrate recommendation, received the top grade, and was appointed magistrate of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，累擢中書舍人，數糾駁偽官。

translations.literal: During the Shenlong era he was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat drafter and many times impeached false officeholders.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era he was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat drafter and many times impeached holders of false offices.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部、黃門侍郎、脩文館學士。

translations.literal: He served successively as vice minister of Personnel, vice minister of the Palace Gate, and scholar of the Xiuzwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as vice minister of Personnel, vice minister of the Palace Gate, and scholar of the Xiuzwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 坐親累，降工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Due to implication in a kinsman's offense, he was demoted to vice director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was implicated in a kinsman's offense, he was demoted to vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 進尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 附太平公主，主誅，玄宗欲捕斬藏用，顧未執政，意解，乃流新州。

translations.literal: Having attached himself to Princess Taiping, when the princess was executed, Emperor Xuanzong wished to capture and execute Cangyong; but seeing that he had not yet held power, his anger eased, and Lu was banished to Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Having attached himself to Princess Taiping, when the princess was executed, Emperor Xuanzong wished to capture and execute Cangyong. But reflecting that Cangyong had not yet held real power, he relented and banished him to Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 或告謀反，推無狀，流州。

translations.literal: Someone reported a plot of rebellion; investigation found no grounds; he remained in exile in the province.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that he was plotting rebellion, but investigation found no evidence, and he remained in exile.

sentences.zh: 會交趾叛，藏用有捍禦勞，改昭州司戶參軍，遷黔州長史，判都督事，卒於始興。

translations.literal: When Jiaozhi rebelled, Cangyong had merit in defense; his sentence was changed to registrar of Zhaozhou, then he was promoted to administrator of Qianzhou, acting as regional commander, and died at Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiaozhi rebelled, Cangyong earned merit in defense. His sentence was reduced, and he was appointed registrar of Zhaozhou, then promoted to administrator of Qianzhou with authority over regional affairs. He died at Shixing.

sentences.zh: 藏用善蓍龜九宮術，工草隸、大小篆、八分，善琴、弈，思精遠，士貴其多能。

translations.literal: Cangyong was skilled in yarrow divination, tortoise oracle, and the nine-palace art; excelled in cursive script, clerical script, large and small seal script, and eight-part script; was adept at zithers and go; his thought was refined and far-reaching—scholars prized his many talents.
translations.idiomatic: Cangyong was skilled in yarrow divination, tortoise oracle, and the nine-palace method. He excelled in cursive script, clerical script, large and small seal script, and eight-part script, and was adept at the zither and go. His thought was refined and far-reaching, and scholars prized his many talents.

sentences.zh: 嘗以俗徇陰陽拘畏，乖至理，泥變通，有國者所不宜專。

translations.literal: He once argued that custom's submission to yin-yang taboos and fearful restrictions departs from supreme principle, clings rigidly to change and adaptation, and is something a state-holder ought not to rely upon exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: He once argued that submitting to yin-yang taboos and fearful restrictions, clinging rigidly to custom and losing sight of change and adaptation, departs from supreme principle and is something no ruler ought to rely on exclusively.

sentences.zh: 謂：「天道從人者也。

translations.literal: He said, "The Way of Heaven follows mankind."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The Way of Heaven follows mankind."

sentences.zh: 古為政者，刑獄不濫則人壽，賦斂省則人富，法令有常則邦寧，賞罰中則兵強。

translations.literal: Ancient rulers: when punishments and prisons were not abused, people lived long; when levies were kept spare, people grew rich; when laws and orders were constant, the realm was at peace; when rewards and punishments were balanced, armies were strong.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient rulers knew that when punishments and prisons were not abused, people lived long; when levies were kept light, people grew rich; when laws and orders were stable, the realm was secure; and when rewards and punishments were balanced, armies were strong.

sentences.zh: 禮者士所歸，賞者士所死，禮賞不倦，則士爭先，否者，雖揆時行罰，涓日出號，無成功矣。

translations.literal: Ritual is what gentlemen rally to; reward is what gentlemen die for—when ritual and reward never slacken, gentlemen strive to be first; otherwise, though one measures the times and metes out punishments, issuing proclamations day by day, there will be no success.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual is what gentlemen rally to, and reward is what gentlemen die for. When ritual and reward never slacken, gentlemen strive to be first. Otherwise, though one measures the times and metes out punishments, issuing proclamations day by day, there will be no success.

sentences.zh: 故任賢使能，不時日而利；

translations.literal: Thus, appointing the worthy and employing the able brings benefit without waiting for auspicious days;
translations.idiomatic: Thus, appointing the worthy and employing the able brings benefit without waiting for auspicious days;

sentences.zh: 明法審令，不卜筮而吉；

translations.literal: clarifying laws and examining orders brings good fortune without divining by oracle;
translations.idiomatic: clarifying laws and examining orders brings good fortune without divination;

sentences.zh: 養勞貴功，不禱祠而福。

translations.literal: nurturing toil and honoring merit brings blessings without prayer and sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: and nurturing toil and honoring merit brings blessings without prayer and sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 」乃為《析滯論》以暢其方，世謂「知言」。

translations.literal: He therefore wrote "On Dispelling Stagnation" to expound his method; the age called it "words of insight."
translations.idiomatic: He therefore wrote "On Dispelling Stagnation" to expound his views, and his contemporaries called it "words of insight."

sentences.zh: 子昂、貞固前死，藏用撫其孤有恩，人稱能終始交。

translations.literal: Zi'ang and Zhengong had died earlier; Cangyong cared for their orphans with kindness—people praised him for friendship maintained from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Zi'ang and Zhengong had died earlier, but Cangyong cared for their orphans with kindness, and people praised him for maintaining friendship from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 始隱山中時，有意當世，人目為「隨駕隱士」。

translations.literal: When he first hid in the mountains, he had his eye on the age—people regarded him as "the hermit who rides along with the imperial carriage."
translations.idiomatic: When he first lived in seclusion in the mountains, he still had his eye on public office, and people regarded him as "the hermit who rides along with the imperial carriage."

sentences.zh: 晚乃徇權利，務為驕縱，素節盡矣。

translations.literal: In his later years he pursued power and profit, striving after arrogance and indulgence—all his former integrity was gone.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he pursued power and profit, striving after arrogance and indulgence, until all his former integrity was gone.

sentences.zh: 司馬承禎嘗召至闕下，將還山，藏用指終南曰：「此中大有嘉處。

translations.literal: Sima Chengzhen once summoned him to the palace gates; as he was about to return to the mountains, Cangyong pointed to Mount Zhongnan and said, "In these hills there are many fine places."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Chengzhen once summoned him to the palace. As Chengzhen was about to return to the mountains, Cangyong pointed to Mount Zhongnan and said, "In these hills there are many fine places."

sentences.zh: 」承禎徐曰：「以仆視之，仕宦之捷徑耳。

translations.literal: Chengzhen slowly replied, "As I see it, they are but a shortcut to office and rank."
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhen replied slowly, "As I see it, they are but a shortcut to office and rank."

sentences.zh: 」藏用慚。

translations.literal: Cangyong was ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Cangyong was ashamed.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons.

sentences.zh: 弟若虛，多才博物。

translations.literal: Younger brother Ruoxu was multitalented and broadly learned in things.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ruoxu was multitalented and broadly learned.

sentences.zh: 隴西辛怡諫為職方，有獲異鼠者，豹首虎臆，大如拳。

translations.literal: Xin Yijian of Longxi, while serving in the Bureau of Appointments, obtained a strange rat with a leopard's head and tiger's chest, as large as a fist.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin Yijian of Longxi served in the Bureau of Appointments, someone captured a strange rat with a leopard's head and tiger's chest, as large as a fist.

sentences.zh: 怡諫謂之鼮鼠而賦之。

translations.literal: Yijian called it a tingshu rat and composed a rhapsody on it.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian called it a tingshu rat and composed a rhapsody on it.

sentences.zh: 若虛曰：「非也，此許慎所謂鼨鼠，豹文而形小。

translations.literal: Ruoxu said, "That is not so—this is what Xu Shen called the tongshu rat, leopard-marked and small in form."
translations.idiomatic: Ruoxu said, "That is not so. This is what Xu Shen called the tongshu rat—leopard-marked and small-bodied."

sentences.zh: 」一坐驚服。

translations.literal: The entire gathering was astonished and convinced.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone present was astonished and convinced.

sentences.zh: 終起居郎，集賢院學士。

translations.literal: He ended as master of writing, scholar of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as master of writing and scholar of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 韋巨源，與安石同系，後周京兆尹總曾孫。

translations.literal: Wei Juyuan was of the same lineage as Wei Anshi, a great-grandson of Wei Zong, Jingzhao intendant of Later Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Juyuan belonged to the same lineage as Wei Anshi and was a great-grandson of Wei Zong, Jingzhao intendant under Later Zhou.

sentences.zh: 祖貞伯，襲鄖國公，入隋，改舒國。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhenbo inherited the title Duke of Yun, entered Sui, and the title was changed to Duke of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhenbo inherited the title Duke of Yun; after entering Sui, the title was changed to Duke of Shu.

sentences.zh: 巨源有吏幹，武後時累遷夏官侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: Juyuan possessed administrative talent; during Empress Wu's reign he was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of War and associate director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Cranes Platform.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan possessed administrative talent. During Empress Wu's reign he was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of War and associate chief minister of the Phoenix and Phoenix-Parrot Pavilions.

sentences.zh: 其治委碎無大體，句校省中遺隱，下符斂克不少蠲，雖收其利，然下所怨苦。

translations.literal: His governance was petty and lacked large design; he scrutinized hidden omissions within the departments and sent down orders to collect and levy without granting reductions—though revenue was gathered, those below resented and suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was petty and lacked broad vision. He scrutinized hidden omissions within the departments and issued orders to collect levies without granting reductions. Though revenue was gathered, those below resented and suffered bitterly.

sentences.zh: 坐李昭德累，貶鄜州刺史。

translations.literal: Punished through implication in Li Zhaode's case, he was demoted to prefect of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Punished through implication in Li Zhaode's case, he was demoted to prefect of Fu.

sentences.zh: 累拜地官尚書。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，以吏部尚書同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he served as minister of Personnel with third rank equal to the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shenlong he served as minister of Personnel with third rank equal to the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 時要官缺，執政以次用其親，巨源秉筆，當除十人，楊再思得其一，試問余授，皆諸宰相近屬。

translations.literal: When important posts were vacant, those in power used their kin in turn; Juyuan held the brush and was to appoint ten men—Yang Zaisi got one—and when the rest were asked about, all were close kin of the various chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: When important posts fell vacant, those in power appointed their kin in turn. Juyuan held the brush for ten appointments—Yang Zaisi received one—and when the remaining posts were named, all went to close kin of the chancellors.

sentences.zh: 再思喟然曰：「吾等誠負天下。

translations.literal: Zaisi sighed and said, "We have truly failed all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Zaisi sighed and said, "We have truly failed the realm."

sentences.zh: 」巨源曰：「時當爾耳。

translations.literal: Juyuan said, "The times are simply like this."
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan said, "The times are simply like this."

sentences.zh: 」是時雖賢有德，終莫得進，士大夫莫不解體。

translations.literal: At that time, though men were worthy and virtuous, none could advance in the end, and scholar-officials were all disheartened.
translations.idiomatic: Though worthy and virtuous men existed, none could advance, and scholar-officials were utterly disheartened.

sentences.zh: 會安石為中書令，避親罷政事。

translations.literal: When Anshi became director of the Secretariat, Juyuan withdrew from government affairs to avoid conflict of interest with kin.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi became director of the Secretariat, Juyuan left government to avoid conflict of interest with kin.

sentences.zh: 尋遷侍中，舒國公。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to palace attendant and enfeoffed Duke of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to palace attendant and enfeoffed Duke of Shu.

sentences.zh: 韋後與敘昆弟，附屬籍。

translations.literal: Empress Wei treated him as a sworn brother and enrolled him in the imperial clan register.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei treated him as a sworn brother and enrolled him in the imperial clan register.

sentences.zh: 武三思封戶在貝州，屬大水，刺史宋璟議免其租，巨源以為蠶桑可輸，繇是河朔人多流徙者。

translations.literal: Wu Sansi's fief households were in Beizhou; when great floods struck, Prefect Song Jing proposed waiving their rent, but Juyuan held that silkworms and mulberry could still be taxed—hence many in the Hebei region fled and drifted away.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi's fief households lay in Beizhou; when great floods struck, Prefect Song Jing proposed waiving their rent, but Juyuan insisted silkworm and mulberry taxes could still be collected—so many in the Hebei region fled.

sentences.zh: 景龍二年。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jinglong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jinglong.

sentences.zh: 韋後自言衣笥有五色雲，巨源倡其偽，勸中宗宣布天下，帝從其言，因是大赦。

translations.literal: Empress Wei claimed that colored clouds appeared in her clothing chest; Juyuan promoted the fraud and urged Emperor Zhongzong to proclaim it to all under Heaven—the emperor followed his words and therefore proclaimed a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei claimed colored clouds appeared in her clothing chest; Juyuan promoted the fraud and urged Emperor Zhongzong to proclaim it throughout the realm. The emperor followed his advice and proclaimed a great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 巨源見帝昏惑，乃與宗楚客、鄭愔、趙延禧等推處祥妖，陰導韋氏行武後故事。

translations.literal: Seeing the emperor muddled, Juyuan joined Zong Chuke, Zheng Yin, Zhao Yanxi, and others in promoting auspicious and strange portents, secretly guiding the Wei clan to follow Empress Wu's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor muddled, Juyuan joined Zong Chuke, Zheng Yin, Zhao Yanxi, and others in promoting omens and portents, secretly guiding the Wei clan to follow Empress Wu's precedent.

sentences.zh: 俄遷尚書左仆射，仍知政事。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, still directing government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs while still directing government affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝方南郊，巨源請後為亞獻，而自為終獻。

translations.literal: As the emperor was performing the southern suburban sacrifice, Juyuan asked that the empress serve as secondary offerer while he himself served as final offerer.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor performed the southern suburban sacrifice, Juyuan asked that the empress serve as secondary offerer while he himself served as final offerer.

sentences.zh: 及臨淄王平諸韋，家人請避之，巨源曰：「吾大臣，無容見難不赴。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Linzi suppressed the Wei faction, his family urged him to flee; Juyuan said, "I am a great minister—I cannot see difficulty and not go."
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Linzi suppressed the Wei faction, his family urged flight; Juyuan said, "I am a great minister—I cannot see danger and not go."

sentences.zh: 」出都街，亂兵殺之，年八十。

translations.literal: He went out into the capital street and was killed by the mutinous troops at eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He went into the capital street and was killed by mutinous troops at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，贈特進、荊州大都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong acceded, Juyuan was posthumously given special advancement and made regional commander of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong acceded, he was posthumously given special advancement and made regional commander of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 博士李處直請謚為「昭」，戶部員外郎李邕以巨源附武三思為相，托韋後親屬，謚「昭」為非。

translations.literal: Erudite Li Chuzhi requested the posthumous title "Zhao"; assistant director of revenue Li Yong held that because Juyuan had attached himself to Wu Sansi as chancellor and relied on Empress Wei's kin, the title "Zhao" was inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Li Chuzhi requested the posthumous title "Zhao"; assistant director of revenue Li Yong argued that because Juyuan had attached himself to Wu Sansi as chancellor and relied on Empress Wei's kin, "Zhao" was inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 處直執不改，邕列陳其惡，不見用，然世皆直邕。

translations.literal: Chuzhi insisted without change; Yong set forth his crimes in detail but was not heeded—yet the age upheld Yong as in the right.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi insisted without change; Yong set forth his crimes in detail but was not heeded—yet the age upheld Yong as correct.

sentences.zh: 韋氏自安石及武後時宰相待價、巨源皆近親，其族至大官者，又數十人。

translations.literal: From Anshi's time and Empress Wu's chancellors Dai Jia and Juyuan, the Wei clan were all close kin; those of the clan who reached high office numbered several tens more.
translations.idiomatic: From Anshi's time through chancellors Dai Jia and Juyuan under Empress Wu, the Wei were all close kin; dozens more of the clan reached high office.

sentences.zh: 趙彥昭，字奐然，甘州張掖人。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanzhao, courtesy name Haoran, was a native of Zhangye in Gan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanzhao, styled Haoran, came from Zhangye in Gan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父武孟，少遊獵，以所獲饋其母，母泣曰：「汝不好書而敖蕩，吾安望哉？

translations.literal: His father Wumeng in youth roamed hunting and gave his catch to his mother; his mother wept and said, "You do not love books but wander and play—what hope can I place in you?"
translations.idiomatic: His father Wumeng in youth roamed hunting and gave his catch to his mother; his mother wept and said, "You do not love books but wander and play—what hope can I place in you?"

sentences.zh: 」不為食。

translations.literal: She would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: She would not eat.

sentences.zh: 武孟感激，遂力學，淹該書記。

translations.literal: Wumeng was stirred and thereafter studied hard, becoming thoroughly versed in records and writing.
translations.idiomatic: Wumeng was stirred and thereafter studied hard, becoming thoroughly versed in records and writing.

sentences.zh: 自長安丞為右臺侍卿史，著《河西人物志》十篇。

translations.literal: From aide of Chang'an he became attendant censor of the Right Censorate and composed ten chapters of "Biographies of the Western Regions."
translations.idiomatic: From aide of Chang'an he became attendant censor of the Right Censorate and composed ten chapters of "Biographies of the Western Regions."

sentences.zh: 彥昭少豪邁，風骨秀爽。

translations.literal: Yanzhao in youth was bold and high-spirited, with elegant bearing and bright manner.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao in youth was bold and high-spirited, with elegant bearing and bright manner.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，調為南部尉。

translations.literal: After passing the jinshi examination he was appointed aide of the southern bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he was appointed aide of the southern bureau.

sentences.zh: 與郭元振、薛稷、蕭至忠善。

translations.literal: He was friendly with Guo Yuanzhen, Xue Ji, and Xiao Zhizhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was friendly with Guo Yuanzhen, Xue Ji, and Xiao Zhizhong.

sentences.zh: 自新豐丞為左臺監察御史。

translations.literal: From aide of Xinfeng he became investigating censor of the Left Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: From aide of Xinfeng he became investigating censor of the Left Censorate.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，累遷中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: During Jinglong he was repeatedly promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and associate director of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: During Jinglong he was repeatedly promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 金城公主嫁吐蕃，始以紀處訥為使，處訥辭，乃授彥昭。

translations.literal: When Princess Jincheng was married to Tibet, Ji Chuna was first appointed envoy but declined; Yanzhao was then given the mission.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Jincheng was married to Tibet, Ji Chuna was first appointed envoy but declined; Yanzhao was then given the mission.
