sentences.zh: 彥昭顧己處外，恐權寵奪移，不悅。

translations.literal: Yanzhao, seeing himself posted abroad, feared his power and favor would be taken away and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao, seeing himself posted abroad, feared his power and favor would be lost and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 司農卿趙履溫曰：「公天宰，而為一介使，不亦鄙乎！

translations.literal: Director of agriculture Zhao Lüwen said, "You are heaven's chancellor, yet you go as a mere envoy—is that not base!"
translations.idiomatic: Director of agriculture Zhao Lüwen said, "You are heaven's chancellor, yet you go as a mere envoy—is that not base!"

sentences.zh: 」彥昭問計安出，履溫乃為請安樂公主留之，遂以將軍楊矩代。

translations.literal: Yanzhao asked where a plan might come from; Lüwen then had Princess Anle request that he remain, and General Yang Ju was sent in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao asked where a plan might come from; Lüwen then had Princess Anle request that he remain, and General Yang Ju was sent in his place.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，出為宋州刺史，坐累貶歸州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong acceded, he was sent out as prefect of Song and later demoted to Guizhou through accumulated offenses.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong acceded, he was sent out as prefect of Song and later demoted to Guizhou through accumulated offenses.

sentences.zh: 俄授涼州都督，為政嚴，下皆股栗。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed regional commander of Liangzhou; his government was strict and all below trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed regional commander of Liangzhou; his government was strict and all below trembled in fear.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部侍郎，持節按邊。

translations.literal: He entered court as vice minister of Personnel and held commission to inspect the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as vice minister of Personnel and held commission to inspect the frontier.

sentences.zh: 遷御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to chief censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief censor.

sentences.zh: 蕭至忠等誅，郭元振、張說言彥昭與秘謀，改刑部尚書、封耿國公，實封百戶。

translations.literal: When Xiao Zhizhong and others were executed, Guo Yuanzhen and Zhang Yue said Yanzhao had shared in the secret plot; his punishment was changed to minister of Punishments and he was enfeoffed Duke of Geng with a substantive fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Zhizhong and others were executed, Guo Yuanzhen and Zhang Yue said Yanzhao had shared in the secret plot; he was made minister of Punishments and enfeoffed Duke of Geng with a substantive fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 彥昭本以權幸進，中宗時，有巫趙挾鬼道出入禁掖，彥昭以姑事之。

translations.literal: Yanzhao had originally advanced through favor and power; under Emperor Zhongzong a shaman Zhao practiced ghost arts and went in and out of the inner palace—Yanzhao treated her as his aunt.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao had originally advanced through favor and power; under Emperor Zhongzong a shaman Zhao practiced ghost arts within the inner palace—Yanzhao treated her as his aunt.

sentences.zh: 嘗衣婦服，乘車與妻偕謁，其得宰相，巫力也。

translations.literal: He once wore women's dress, rode in a carriage with his wife to call on her together—the shaman's power was how he gained the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: He once wore women's dress and rode with his wife to call on her—the shaman's power was how he gained the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 於是殿中侍御史郭震劾暴舊惡。

translations.literal: Thereupon attendant censor within the palace Guo Zhen impeached and exposed his old crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon palace attendant censor Guo Zhen impeached and exposed his old crimes.

sentences.zh: 會姚崇執政，惡其為人，貶江州別駕，卒。

translations.literal: When Yao Chong took power he detested Yanzhao's character and demoted him to vice prefect of Jiangzhou; he died there.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chong took power he detested Yanzhao's character and demoted him to vice prefect of Jiangzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 和逢堯，岐州岐山人。

translations.literal: He Xianyao was a native of Qishan in Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He Xianyao was a native of Qishan in Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武後時，負鼎詣闕下上書，自言願助天子和飪百度。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's reign he carried a cauldron to the palace gates and submitted a memorial, saying himself that he wished to help the Son of Heaven harmonize the hundred duties.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Wu's reign he carried a cauldron to the palace gates and submitted a memorial, saying he wished to help the Son of Heaven harmonize the hundred duties.

sentences.zh: 有司讓曰：「昔桀不道，伊尹負鼎於湯；

translations.literal: The relevant office reproved him, saying, "In antiquity Jie was without the Way and Yi Yin carried a cauldron to Tang;
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office reproved him: "In antiquity Jie was without the Way and Yi Yin carried a cauldron to Tang;

sentences.zh: 今天子聖明，百司以和，尚何所調？

translations.literal: today the Son of Heaven is sagely and enlightened and the hundred offices are in harmony—what still needs adjusting?"
translations.idiomatic: today the Son of Heaven is sagely and enlightened and the hundred offices are in harmony—what still needs adjusting?"

sentences.zh: 」逢堯不能答，流莊州。

translations.literal: Xianyao could not answer and was banished to Zhuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyao could not answer and was banished to Zhuang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十餘年，乃舉進士高第，累擢監察御史。

translations.literal: After more than ten years he finally passed the jinshi examination in high standing and was repeatedly promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years he passed the jinshi examination in high standing and was repeatedly promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 突厥默啜請尚公主，逢堯以御史中丞攝鴻臚卿，報可。

translations.literal: When the Türkic khan Mohechu requested marriage to a princess, Xianyao as chief investigating censor acting as director of guests for embassies reported approval.
translations.idiomatic: When the Türkic khan Mohechu requested marriage to a princess, Xianyao as chief investigating censor acting director of guests for embassies reported approval.

sentences.zh: 默啜遣貴近頡利來曰：「詔送金鏤具鞍，乃塗金，非天子意。

translations.literal: Mohechu sent a noble close kin named Jieli, who said, "The edict sent a gold-inlaid saddle, yet it is only gold-plated—not the Son of Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Mohechu sent a noble close kin named Jieli, who said, "The edict sent a gold-inlaid saddle, yet it is only gold-plated—not the Son of Heaven's intent.

sentences.zh: 使者不可信，雖得公主，猶非實，請罷和親。

translations.literal: The envoy cannot be trusted; though we obtain the princess it is still not real—please stop the marriage alliance."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy cannot be trusted; though we obtain the princess it is still not genuine—please stop the marriage alliance."

sentences.zh: 」欲馳去，左右色動，逢堯呼曰：「我大國使，不受我辭，可輒去。

translations.literal: He wished to gallop away; those at his side changed color; Xianyao called out, "I am an envoy of the great state—you will not accept my words yet dare to leave at once!"
translations.idiomatic: He wished to gallop away; those at his side changed color; Xianyao called out, "I am an envoy of the great state—you will not accept my words yet dare to leave at once!"

sentences.zh: 」乃牽持其人謂曰：「漢法重女婿而送鞍具，欲安且久，不以金為貴。

translations.literal: He then seized the man and said, "By Han law the son-in-law is honored and the saddle and fittings are sent to settle him in peace and for long—not because gold is prized.
translations.idiomatic: He then seized the man and said, "By Han law the son-in-law is honored and saddle and fittings are sent for lasting peace—not because gold is prized.

sentences.zh: 可汗乃貪金而不貴信邪？

translations.literal: Can the khan covet gold and not prize good faith?"
translations.idiomatic: Can the khan covet gold and not prize good faith?"

sentences.zh: 」默啜聞曰：「漢使至吾國眾矣，斯食鐵石人，不可易。

translations.literal: Mohechu heard and said, "Han envoys have come to my state in great numbers, but this man eats iron and stone—he cannot be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Mohechu heard and said, "Han envoys have come to my state in great numbers, but this man eats iron and stone—he cannot be changed."

sentences.zh: 」因備禮以見。

translations.literal: He therefore prepared full rites to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore prepared full rites to receive him.

sentences.zh: 逢堯說之曰：「天子昔為單於都護，思與可汗通舊好，可汗當向風慕義，襲冠冕，取重諸蕃。

translations.literal: Xianyao persuaded him, saying, "The Son of Heaven formerly served as protector of the khans and wishes to renew old friendship with the khan; the khan should face the wind and admire righteousness, don the cap and robes, and gain weight among the various barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: Xianyao persuaded him: "The Son of Heaven formerly served as protector of the khans and wishes to renew old friendship; the khan should face the wind and admire righteousness, don cap and robes, and gain weight among the barbarians."

sentences.zh: 」默啜信之，為斂發紫衣，南面再拜稱臣，遣子入朝。

translations.literal: Mohechu believed him, put on purple robes, faced south and twice bowed calling himself subject, and sent his son to court.
translations.idiomatic: Mohechu believed him, donned purple robes, faced south and twice bowed calling himself subject, and sent his son to court.

sentences.zh: 逢堯以使有指，擢戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Because the envoy had achieved his aim, Xianyao was promoted to vice minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Because the envoy had achieved his aim, Xianyao was promoted to vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 坐善太平公主，斥朗州司馬，終柘州刺史。

translations.literal: Punished for attachment to Princess Taiping, he was demoted to secretary of Lang Prefecture and ended as prefect of Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for attachment to Princess Taiping, he was demoted to secretary of Lang Prefecture and ended as prefect of Zhe.

sentences.zh: 逢堯詼詭，當大事敢僥福，故卒以附麗廢，然唐興奉使者稱逢堯。

translations.literal: Xianyao was witty and crafty; on great affairs he dared gamble for fortune—hence in the end he was ruined through clinging to power, yet since Tang's rise envoys abroad have praised Xianyao.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyao was witty and crafty; on great affairs he dared gamble for fortune—hence he was ruined through clinging to power, yet since Tang's rise envoys abroad have praised Xianyao.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：異哉，玄宗之器蕭至忠也，不亦惑乎！

translations.literal: The commentator says: How strange—Emperor Xuanzong's esteem for Xiao Zhizhong—is it not confused!
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: How strange—Emperor Xuanzong's esteem for Xiao Zhizhong—is it not confused!

sentences.zh: 至忠本非賢，而寄賢以奸利，失之則邀利以喪賢，姻艷後，挾寵主，取宰相，謀間王室，身誅家破，遺臭無窮。

translations.literal: Zhizhong was originally not worthy, yet he borrowed worth for treacherous profit; when he lost it he courted profit and lost worth; he married into the empress's splendor, relied on her favor as patron, took the chancellorship, and schemed against the royal house—his person was executed, his house destroyed, and his stench endures without end.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong was originally not worthy, yet he borrowed worth for treacherous profit; when he lost it he courted profit and lost worth; he married into the empress's splendor, relied on her favor, took the chancellorship, and schemed against the royal house—his person was executed, his house destroyed, and his infamy endures without end.

sentences.zh: 而帝以乾曜似之，遽使當國，是帝舉不知至忠之不可用，又不知乾曜之所可用也。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor, because Qianyao resembled him, promptly had him direct the state—thus the emperor both did not know Zhizhong could not be used and did not know what in Qianyao could be used.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor, because Qianyao resembled him, promptly had him direct the state—thus the emperor neither knew Zhizhong could not be used nor knew what in Qianyao could be used.

sentences.zh: 或稱帝不以罪掩才，益可怪嘆。

translations.literal: Some praise the emperor for not letting crimes mask talent—this is all the more strange and lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Some praise the emperor for not letting crimes mask talent—this is all the more strange and lamentable.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 力士誠腐夫庸人，不能發擿天子之迷，若曰「至忠賢於初，固不繆於末；

translations.literal: Lishi was truly a rotten petty man who could not expose the Son of Heaven's confusion; had he said, "Zhizhong was worthy at the start and was not wrong at the end; once wrong at the end, he was truly not worthy at the start.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi was truly a rotten petty man who could not expose the Son of Heaven's confusion; had he said, "Zhizhong was worthy at the start and was not wrong at the end; once wrong at the end, he was truly not worthy at the start.

sentences.zh: 既繆於末，果不賢於初。

translations.literal: Having been wrong at the end, he was indeed not worthy at the start.
translations.idiomatic: Having been wrong at the end, he was indeed not worthy at the start.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下圖之」，如是，帝且悟往失而精來鑒已。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty consider this"—then the emperor would have awakened to past error and refined future judgment.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty consider this"—then the emperor would have awakened to past error and refined future judgment.

sentences.zh: 其後相李林甫、將安祿山，皆基於不明，身播岷陬，信自取之歟。

translations.literal: Afterward in appointing Li Linfu and entrusting An Lushan, both sprang from lack of discernment; his person was cast to the remote Min mountains—was it not truly self-wrought?
translations.idiomatic: Afterward in appointing Li Linfu and entrusting An Lushan, both sprang from lack of discernment; his person was cast to the remote Min mountains—was it not truly self-wrought?
